I will plant my own traditional cassava and yam cuttings saved from last season because the improved seeds sold in town are too expensive for a smallholder like me. My children and I will do all the labor ourselves from clearing to harvest, so I will not hire any outside workers that I cannot afford to pay. I will spread cow manure on the mounds because I keep animals and it costs nothing, but I will not buy chemical fertilizer or sprays this year since the government subsidy rarely reaches our village. We depend entirely on the April-to-October rains, so irrigation is not something I consider on this upland plot.
